trials_detail.reason: Identifies that a finite-chain axial clamp measures the logarithmic derivative of the endpoint marginal, and replaces the supplied inverse-Langevin force with the derivative of an N-fold uniform-projection density. The physical force sign and 1/b scaling are correct in the final source. An initial np.math API error is exposed by a clamp check and repaired with Python math before final tests. The unrelated git-diff command fails because /app is not a repository; later public tests and a 54-case clamp sweep succeed. All seven private checks pass with hidden errors below .00016515. This is a correct physical solution, not retention of the source closure.

Recognizes the finite-N endpoint-marginal force before editing, fits the force-mode calibration, and implements the physical polynomial log derivative. The first implementation omits 1/b when converting its dimensionless derivative. The emitted edge-case review explicitly diagnoses this units error and corrects it before final submission; the final source has derivative/(density*length), and its finite-difference check and all seven private checks pass. Earlier calibration-key, root-at-zero, patch and git commands are resolved scratch issues. They are not a final mathematical or physical failure.

Explicitly derives the uniform projected-step convolution and its finite-N clamp log derivative, then uses reflection to the lower half of the Irwin-Hall coordinate to control cancellation. The final derivative includes the correct 1/(2b) coordinate conversion and force sign. Weighted fitting recovers b accurately; a public full-domain grid is finite and all seven private checks pass. A failed git-status command and an invalid initial patch are resolved without affecting the final submission. This is a correct physical solution.
